2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are inter alia that the opposite party No. 1 being pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case (Pre-emption) No. 82 of 1985 before the Court of the learned Munsif now Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chattogram under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, in short, 'the SAT Act'. The contentions of the petitioners briefly are that the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 5 purchased entire land of the case holding by virtue of Certificate Case No. 17440/60-61 on 18-7-1961 and obtained possession accordingly and later on, transferred 177 decimals of land on 5-7-1984 in favour of the pre-emptor by dint of a registered sale deed and also made over possession to him and thus the pre-emptor became co-sharer of the holding by way of purchase. The pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-4 are strangers in the case holding. They purchased the case land on 3-3-1985 by virtue of a registered deed. The pre-emptor was not aware as to the aforesaid sale deed and after that, being aware as to the sale of the case land on 3-9-1985, he procured the certificate copy of the impugned sale deed on 12-9-1985 and came to know that the opposite party No. 5 transferred the case land to the opposite party Nos. 1-4 and thereafter, instituted aforesaid pre-emption case after observing all the formalities. 

 16. He next submits that the learned Advocate for the pre-emptee-petitioners who referred to the written statement filed by the opposite party No. 4(ka) stated that certain persons were not impleaded as there is no co-sharer of the auction purchaser Yunus Talukder, therefore, the question of impleading them as party does not arise at all. 

 19. The learned Senior Assistant Judge dismissed the pre-emption case mainly on the ground that the pre-emption case is bad for defect of parties. The Appellate Court after delving into the facts and law and considering the evidence on record held that since the pre-emptee-opposite party purchased the case land only mentioning RS Plot of the case holding and all the sharers of the RS Record were made parties. Therefore, the record owners of the BS Survey are not required to be made parties. Since at the time of institution of the case, B.S Survey had not been started, the pre-emptee contended that the impugned deed was not aout and outsale deed, but a deed of disclaimer, therefore, the pre-emption case is not maintainable. But the Appellate Court as a last court of fact thoroughly examined the evidence on record rightly held that all the co-sharers of the R.S holding i.e. case holding were made parties, therefore, there is no necessity to implead the co-sharers of the latest khatian which was prepared after institution of the pre-emption case. In the written objection, the pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-4 under paragraph No. 6 stated to the effect: "প্রার্থীকের মোকদ্দমা পক্ষদোষে সম্পূর্ণরুপে অচল।” 

 20. And under paragraph No.18, the pre-emptee also stated: "নালিশী খতিয়ানের সমস্ত স্বার্থসংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিগণকে পক্ষ করা ছাড়া অত্র মোকদ্দমা অচল।”
